title: They thought it was the end of him.
paragraphs: They thought it was the end of him.

The pit was too deep.
The betrayal was too personal.
The silence from heaven was too loud.
And if we’re honest… some of us have stood in that same darkness, wondering if God forgot our name.
Before God ever promoted Joseph, He allowed him to be stripped, sold, lied about, and forgotten.
That part doesn’t get preached enough.
Because we love the palace, but we don’t talk about the pit.

Genesis tells it plainly, without softening the blow. “וַיִּפְשִׁיטוּ אֶת־יוֹסֵף אֶת־כֻּתָּנְתּוֹ” (Vayafshitu et-Yosef et-kuttoneto) — “And they stripped Joseph of his robe” (Genesis 37:23). That robe wasn’t just clothing. It was identity. Favor. Promise.
And God let it be taken.
Sit with that.

God didn’t stop the brothers.
God didn’t block the betrayal.
God didn’t interrupt the injustice.
Because sometimes the very thing you think is destroying your calling… is actually preparing it.

Joseph didn’t go from dream to destiny.
He went from dream to devastation.
Thrown into a pit. “הַבּוֹר רֵק אֵין בּוֹ מָיִם” (habbor req, ein bo mayim) — “The pit was empty; there was no water in it” (Genesis 37:24). No water. No life. No comfort.
Just silence.
Have you ever prayed and felt that kind of silence?
Like your words hit the ceiling and fell back on your chest?
Be honest. This hit harder than you expected.
Because some of you are there right now. Not in a literal pit, but in a season that feels empty. Dry. Confusing.
And you’re asking, “God, what did I do wrong?”
Joseph did nothing wrong.
Let that break something inside you that needed to be broken.
He was faithful. Obedient. Pure-hearted.
And still… he was sold.
“וַיִּמְכְּרוּ אֶת־יוֹסֵף” (vayimkeru et-Yosef) — “They sold Joseph” (Genesis 37:28).
Thirty pieces of silver would later echo in another betrayal. Another innocent man. Another story where it looked like evil was winning.
But heaven was writing something deeper.

Joseph’s life was not falling apart.
It was falling into place.
But you don’t see that when you’re in chains.
In Potiphar’s house, Joseph served. In prison, Joseph interpreted dreams. And the Scripture whispers something that changes everything:
“וַיהוָה הָיָה עִם־יוֹסֵף” (Adonai hayah im-Yosef) — “The LORD was with Joseph” (Genesis 39:2).

With him… in slavery.
With him… in false accusation.
With him… in prison.

God’s presence is not proven by comfort.
It’s proven by purpose.
Even in the Greek Septuagint, the idea holds: “Κύριος ἦν μετὰ Ἰωσήφ” (Kyrios ēn meta Iōsēph) — “The Lord was with Joseph.”
Not occasionally. Not when things improved.
With him.
Right there in the injustice.
Right there in the waiting.
Right there in the silence you thought meant abandonment.
If that doesn’t wake something up in your spirit… read it again.
Because we’ve been taught a dangerous lie — that God’s favor means ease.
Joseph’s life proves the opposite.
Favor will put you in places where your character is tested, your faith is stretched, and your trust in God is refined like fire.
Before the throne… there was a prison.
Before authority… there was accusation.
Before elevation… there was humiliation.
And some of you want what Joseph had… but you’re resisting what Joseph endured.

Because the truth is, God is not ignoring you.
He is developing you.
There’s a Hebrew weight to the word “tested” — “נָסָה” (nasah). It means to prove, to try, to refine.
God wasn’t punishing Joseph.
He was proving him.
There is a difference.
And when the moment finally came… it happened suddenly.
One day he was forgotten in prison.
The next day, Pharaoh was calling his name.
That’s how God moves.
Quiet for a long time… then everything shifts in a moment.
“וַיְרִיצֻהוּ מִן־הַבּוֹר” (vayeritzuhu min-habor) — “They quickly brought him out of the pit” (Genesis 41:14).
Quickly.
After years of waiting… suddenly.
That’s the part people don’t understand.
God is never late. He is precise.
And when Joseph stood before Pharaoh, he didn’t take credit.
“It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace” (Genesis 41:16).
That’s the man the pit produced.
Not arrogant. Not bitter. Not broken beyond repair.
Refined.
And that’s when God trusted him with influence.
Promotion is not about gifting.
It’s about character.
And God will never elevate what hasn’t been tested.

So if you’re in a season where nothing makes sense…
where people walked away…
where doors closed…
where your prayers feel unanswered…
You are not buried.
You are planted.
And planted things don’t look like they’re growing… until they break through.
Not for today, but for the day when your faith feels weak and you need to remember what God is doing behind the scenes.
Not because we’re selling something cheap, but because we’re building something eternal.
If you truly want to glorify God… don’t just consume truth. Help carry it.
Because this isn’t just content.
This is calling.
This is rescue.
This is the moment someone decides not to give up.
The pit didn’t cancel Joseph.
It revealed him.
